Q5423108.note: Fryxell's history of Charles XII states that Stuart chose the land of Toberup (also written Tiberup) north of Humlebæk, between Helsingør and Copenhagen, as the landing place. Swedish troops came ashore there against Danish entrenchments on the beach. The atlas point is the gazetteer node for the village of Tibberup in Helsingør municipality, a sector reference for the landing beach on the Øresund shore just to the east. It is not a surveyed boat-landing point, a Danish battery position or the later Swedish camp. The existing Gregorian date is retained; the Swedish-calendar 25 July in the source corresponds to it. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

Q5722624.note: Radio Habana Cuba describes Antonio Maceo's invading column camping at the settlement of Las Taironas on 17 January 1896 and meeting a Spanish force that held positions on the nearby road from Pinar del Río to La Coloma, including a bridge, buildings and roadside ditches. The Calendario Cubano entry quotes the invasion diaries placing the combat at Las Taironas at the gates of Pinar del Río. The atlas point is the gazetteer node for the Las Taironas hamlet south-east of the city; it is a settlement-sector reference, not the Spanish road position or either column's line. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred; figures quoted in the sources are not adopted.

Q13403439.note: Reviewed location: Songshan (Mount Song) in Lameng township, Longling County, Yunnan, the fortified mountain attacked by the Chinese Expeditionary Force from 4 June 1944 until its capture on 7 September 1944, as dated on the Longling County government portal. The Baoshan government records the battle site as a national key cultural relic protection unit. The point is the OpenStreetMap feature for that named battle site at Dayakou, on the Burma Road loop around the mountain. It is a site reference, not the summit bunker, a trench line or any unit position. The existing dates are retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

Q55647639.note: The Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University, Patiala) states that Jahan Khan's troops lay in wait for Baba Dip Singh's force near Gohlvar village, 8 km beyond Tarn Taran, where a fierce action took place. The fighting then carried on towards Ramsar and the precincts of the Harimandar in Amritsar, where Dip Singh fell. The atlas point anchors the Gohlvar action using the gazetteer node for Gohlwar village. It does not locate the later stages in Amritsar, either force's position or the full engagement. The existing month-precision date is retained; the encyclopaedia gives 11 November 1757. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred; the encyclopaedia's figure for the Sikh force is not adopted.
